To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified eight novel mutations in the PCS1 gene in extremely obese individuals, which have been confirmed to cause a mild form of obesity in hetero- and homozygous carriers, and that we have identified the first genetic risk factors for obesity in children.

we found eight new heterozygous mutations causing partial PCS1/3 deficiency, that these mutations are rare and are present in 8.3% of extremely obese individuals, and that carriers of these mutations are at higher risk of being obese.
heterozygous mutations in the PCS1 gene, encoding a key protein in the regulation of food intake and energy homeostasis, contribute to common human obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel mutations in the PCS1/3 gene and their prevalence in a European population.
the identification and functional characterization of rare mutations in the PCS1 gene in extremely obese subjects.
the identification of novel heterozygous mutations that contribute to obesity and provides evidence for an additive effect of these mutations on the risk of obesity.

heterozygous mutations of PCSK1 are a rare cause of human obesity.

mutations causing partial PCS1/3 deficiency increase the risk of obesity in a dose-dependent manner.
heterozygous mutations causing partial PCSPC1/3 deficiency contribute to human obesity.
heterozygous mutations in the PCS1 gene are associated with obesity in humans.
